function.arguments: {"finding": "The severity distribution differs between male and female patients in the treatment arm: women are more likely to have mild (35 vs 23) and less likely to have moderate (46 vs 54) severity. This imbalance could confound the observed response-rate difference. However, the difference in response rates is in the same direction (men better) across all severity strata: in mild, F (97.1%) > M (91.3%); in moderate, F (67.4%) ≈ M (68.5%); in severe, F (30.4%) < M (49.0%). The overall difference is driven by the severe group, where men have a higher response rate. The weighted average (by severity) yields the same difference as the raw rate, confirming that the imbalance does not reverse the sign. Thus, the observed difference is robust to confounding by severity.", "implication": "The confounding by severity does not change the direction of the difference — men still have a higher response rate.
